topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The opening introduces the final lecture on cancer therapy and outlines its main learning objectives.

topics.label: Conventional modalities: surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: They cover established, non-targeted approaches to cancer treatment that physically remove tumors, irradiate tissue, or broadly damage dividing cells.

topics.label: Exploiting cancer cell vulnerabilities, checkpoint defects, and DNA repair deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: They examine therapeutic strategies that exploit intrinsic weaknesses of cancer cells, including hormone dependence, cell cycle checkpoint failures, and DNA repair defects.

topics.label: Kinase inhibitors, oncogene addiction, and resistance mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: They detail the principles of targeting hyperactivated oncogenic kinases with small-molecule inhibitors and the mechanisms by which tumors develop drug resistance and addiction.

topics.label: Monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: They discuss targeted therapeutics that use engineered antibodies to disrupt oncogenic signaling, trigger cytotoxic immune responses, or deliver toxins directly to tumor cells.

topics.label: Tumor immunology, checkpoint blockade, and cell-based immunotherapies
topics.groupedBecause: They address the principles of cancer immune surveillance and the development of immunotherapies, including checkpoint inhibitors, bispecific engagers, and CAR T cells.

topics.label: Clinical challenges, historical progress, and future directions in cancer therapy
topics.groupedBecause: They evaluate broader trends in cancer survival and prevention, ongoing therapeutic challenges such as tumor heterogeneity, and future directions and ethical considerations in treatment.
